terms.def: A non-horizontal line <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = mx + b</annotation></semantics></math> that the graph approaches as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \to \pm\infty</annotation></semantics></math>; a rational function has one when the numerator's degree is one more than the denominator's.

The change in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> divided by the change in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> between two points of a line, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}</annotation></semantics></math>. A line has the same slope between any two of its points.

A multiple of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose sine and cosine are known exactly from the special right triangles. Its reference angle, the acute angle between its terminal ray and the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, gives the size of each value; the quadrant gives the sign.

One of the two right triangles whose sides are known exactly from one side: the 45-45-90 triangle, with sides in the ratio <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the 30-60-90 triangle, with sides <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 : \sqrt{3} : 2</annotation></semantics></math> (the short leg across from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>).

An angle placed with its vertex at the origin and its initial ray along the positive <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis. It turns to its terminal ray, counterclockwise for a positive angle and clockwise for a negative one.

The sum and difference identities <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>±</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(a \pm b)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>±</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sin a\cos b \pm \cos a\sin b</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>±</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(a \pm b)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∓</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos a\cos b \mp \sin a\sin b</annotation></semantics></math>, and the double-angle identities <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2a) = 2\sin a\cos a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(2a)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos^2 a - \sin^2 a</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\cos^2 a - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 - 2\sin^2 a</annotation></semantics></math> that follow from them.

Two or more equations with the same unknowns, to be solved together. A solution makes every equation true at once. Two lines that cross have one solution; parallel lines have none; the same line has infinitely many.

The function <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math>: the slope of the terminal ray of the angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Its period is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, its zeros are at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = k\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, and it has vertical asymptotes at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, where cosine is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>.

A matrix whose entry in row i, column j is the chance of moving from state j to state i in one step, so each column adds up to 1. A state vector lists how many (or what share) are in each state; with T the transition matrix, one step later it is T times the state vector, n steps later Tⁿ times it, and one step earlier T⁻¹ times it.

An equation or inequality in which the unknown is the input of a trigonometric function, such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(2x) \le 0</annotation></semantics></math>. It usually has two solutions per period; to find all of them in an interval, isolate the function, take the principal value, use symmetry for the second angle, and add periods.

An equation with trigonometric functions that is true for every input where both sides are defined, such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Identities let you replace an expression with an equivalent one to find exact values, simplify, or solve equations.

A ratio of two sides of a right triangle, named from an acute angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>opposite</mtext><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>opposite</mtext><mtext>adjacent</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}</annotation></semantics></math> (SOH CAH TOA). It depends only on the angle, not on the size of the triangle.

The circle of radius 1 centered at the origin, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + y^2 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. The terminal ray of an angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> in standard position meets it at the point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.

A quantity with a magnitude and a direction, written ⟨a, b⟩ or ai + bj: it moves a units across and b units up. Its magnitude is √(a² + b²). Vectors add component by component, a scalar multiple kv scales the length by |k|, a unit vector has length 1, and the dot product ⟨a, b⟩ · ⟨c, d⟩ = ac + bd is 0 for perpendicular vectors.

A function that gives a vector for each input, p(t) = ⟨x(t), y(t)⟩ = x(t)i + y(t)j. Drawn from the origin, p(t) is the position vector of the point (x(t), y(t)), and its tip traces the parametric curve. p(t2) − p(t1) is the displacement, and dividing by t2 − t1 gives the average rate of change vector.

The turning point of a parabola, at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -\frac{b}{2a}</annotation></semantics></math>. In vertex form <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = a(x - h)^2 + k</annotation></semantics></math> the vertex is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(h, k)</annotation></semantics></math>.

terms.def: A vertical line <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = a</annotation></semantics></math> near which a function's outputs increase or decrease without bound. A rational function has one where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - a)</annotation></semantics></math> divides the denominator more times than the numerator.

A stretch or compression of a graph. A vertical dilation <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = af(x)</annotation></semantics></math> multiplies every output by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>; a horizontal dilation <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = f(bx)</annotation></semantics></math> multiplies every input by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{b}</annotation></semantics></math>.

A shift of a graph without changing its shape. A vertical translation <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = f(x) + k</annotation></semantics></math> moves every output <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> units up; a horizontal translation <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = f(x - h)</annotation></semantics></math> moves the graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> units right.

The point where a graph crosses the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, f(0))</annotation></semantics></math>. A function has at most one.

An input <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(a) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. On the graph, a zero is an <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-intercept, the point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>.
